The aim of our charge is love from a pure heart, a good conscience and sincere faith. How is that aim seen in you?
Paul calls himself the foremost of sinners, yet he received mercy. What does Paul's story tell you about God's patience?
"Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners." How does this simple truth speak to you?
Paul urges Timothy to hold faith and a good conscience. How do you keep your conscience clear?
Paul urges prayers for everyone, including leaders. Who could you pray for that you usually forget?
There is one mediator between God and people, the man Christ Jesus. What does it mean that Jesus stands between us and God?
Paul speaks of lifting holy hands without anger or quarrelling. What helps you pray with a peaceful heart?
Paul lists what makes a good overseer. Which quality would you like to grow in?
Deacons must hold the mystery of the faith with a clear conscience. Why does character matter for those who serve?
Paul describes the mystery of godliness: Christ revealed in the flesh. What part of this hymn moves you?
Everything created by God is good when received with thanksgiving. What can you thank God for today?
Paul says godliness is of value in every way. How are you training yourself for godliness?
"Let no one despise you for your youth, but set an example." How can you set an example in speech, conduct and love?
Paul says to treat older and younger people as family. How can your church feel like family?
Paul gives instruction for caring for widows. Who in your church needs care and practical help?
Paul talks about honouring those who lead well. How can you honour your church leaders?
"Godliness with contentment is great gain." Where do you need contentment?
Paul says to flee these things and pursue righteousness, faith and love. What do you need to flee or pursue?
Paul praises God who alone has immortality and dwells in unapproachable light. What does this show about God?
Those who are rich should be generous and ready to share. How can you be rich in good works?
